name: Thresher's Coif
description: A hood of quilted roughspun with a band of grain sacking sewn inside the brim. A thresher works from dark to dark and knows the trick of finding one more hour in a body that has none left.

name: Fisher's Netted Cowl
description: Knotted river net stiffened with pitch and hung over a leather cap. Whatever swings at the wearer tends to find itself tangled, the way everything eventually does around a fisher.

name: Tanner's Layered Jerkin
description: Nine hides pressed and stitched into one, each layer cured a little harder than the last. A tanner will tell you that leather learns from every blow it takes.

name: Miner's Ironback Plate
description: Deep seam ore hammered flat and riveted over a soot stained coat. The metal still remembers the pressure it came out of, and it drinks a share of every blow rather than passing it on.

name: Herbalist's Greenstep Boots
description: Soft boots bound with living greenweave that never quite dries out. Something in the lining keeps working while the wearer stands still, the way a garden does at night.

name: Courier's Longstride Boots
description: Road worn leather, resoled so many times the original boot is a rumour. A courier who is never caught arrives with all the speed of the road still in them.

name: Mason's Keystone Boots
description: Heavy boots with dressed stone sewn into the heel, mortar dust worked permanently into the seams. A mason plants their feet once and the whole wall goes up true.

name: Glassblower's Lantern Shield
description: A round frame of kiln iron panelled with mirror glass, the panes thick as a thumb. The first strike of any fight goes into the glass instead of the arm behind it.

name: Watchman's Bell Buckler
description: A small iron buckler with the night watch bell riveted to the boss. It rings when it is struck, and a watchman who is losing rings it louder.

name: Chandler's Waxlight Buckler
description: Tallow poured into a shallow iron dish and wicked at the rim, carried like a shield. When trouble opens a door, the wick takes the draught and flares.
